name: Rhode Island veterans: Office of Veterans Services (RIVETS) Veterans Resource Center
organization: Rhode Island Office of Veterans Services (RIVETS)
description: The statewide Veterans Resource Center in Warwick offers benefits counseling, help with discharge papers and help applying for VA and state programs, plus case management for housing, employment, transportation, health and food needs. Veterans, service members, Guard, Reserve and their families can use it.
next_step: Call 401-921-2119, or complete the RIVets Intake Form on vets.ri.gov to have a representative contact you.
constraints: RIVETS is a state office, not the VA Regional Office or a VA medical center.

name: The Point: Rhode Island Aging and Disability Resource Center
organization: Rhode Island Office of Healthy Aging, with United Way of Rhode Island
description: One statewide line, answered around the clock, for people 55 and older, adults with disabilities and caregivers: help finding services and applying for public and private programs. Interpreters are available. Military service is not required.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

name: Medicare counseling (Rhode Island SHIP)
organization: Rhode Island Office of Healthy Aging, State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP)
description: Free, unbiased Medicare counseling from Rhode Island’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, through the Office of Healthy Aging and partner agencies across the state, including senior centers in Johnston, Pawtucket, South Kingstown (Wakefield) and Westerly and community agencies in Woonsocket, East Providence, Central Falls and Newport.
next_step: Call the SHIP line at 1-888-884-8721, or call the Point at 401-462-4444. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Counseling is by appointment. Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

name: Rhode Island Long-Term Care Ombudsman and elder abuse reporting
organization: Office of the Rhode Island State Long Term Care Ombudsman; Rhode Island Office of Healthy Aging, Adult Protective Services
description: Advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and other care facilities, including reports of suspected abuse in a facility. The Office of Healthy Aging’s Adult Protective Services takes reports of abuse, neglect, financial exploitation or self-neglect of people 60 and older living in the community.
next_step: Call the ombudsman at 401-785-3340 or toll-free 888-351-0808. To report abuse of an older person at home, call Adult Protective Services at 401-462-0555, any time; reports can be anonymous. If someone is in immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

name: Free and low-cost legal help for older Rhode Islanders
organization: Rhode Island Legal Services; Rhode Island Bar Association
description: The Office of Healthy Aging lists two legal partners for people 60 and older: Rhode Island Legal Services gives free legal help to lower-income adults 60+ with public-assistance programs, and the Rhode Island Bar Association offers legal help to adults 60+ with fees on a sliding scale.
next_step: Call Rhode Island Legal Services at 401-274-2652 or 800-662-5034. For other legal questions, ask the Point (401-462-4444) for the Bar Association’s senior program.
constraints: Legal aid screens by age, income and case type.

name: VA health care in Rhode Island
organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Providence Healthcare System
description: Rhode Island veterans are served by the VA Providence Healthcare System: the Providence VA Medical Center (830 Chalkstone Avenue, Providence; 401-273-7100) and its community clinics. The Warwick Vet Center (2038 Warwick Ave.; 401-739-0167) offers readjustment counseling.
next_step: Call 401-273-7100 or the local VA call center, 401-457-3336, for appointments. Not enrolled yet? Ask RIVETS for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.

name: Ocean State Center for Independent Living
organization: Ocean State Center for Independent Living
description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
Warwick office (Kent County): 1944 Warwick Avenue, Warwick, RI 02889; TTY 401-738-1015.
Pawtucket office (Providence County): 175 Main Street, Pawtucket; same phone.

name: Veterans Inc.: veteran housing help (SSVF)
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 12-ZZ-041): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you. A second intake number is listed: 508-791-1213.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
